title: QBR Risk Sprint & Save Playbook — Customer Renewal Assessment Template
body:
Purpose:
This working doc is a compact QBR-aligned risk assessment and execution playbook for customers approaching renewal (60->0 days). It's meant to live alongside standard renewal tracking but focused on a 'risk sprint' — short, prioritized interventions to recover at-risk renewals and create an escalation path when mitigation alone is insufficient.

Audience:
- Customer Success Managers (CSMs) and Renewal Specialists
- Solutions Engineering (SE) and Sales Ops support for technical mitigations
- Customer Success leadership and Execs for escalations

How to use this doc (quick):
1) At -60 days run the initial risk score using the rubric below. Add to the QBR agenda if score >= 30 (flagged).
2) If flagged, run the 14-day sprint plan: owner assignments, 3 primary save plays, stakeholder outreach cadence.
3) If no progress at -14 days escalate per the matrix and prepare the Exec Briefing packet for -7 days.
4) Track all interventions on the renewal ticket and update the "escalation outcome" section after final customer decision.

QBR Agenda Template (30–45 min) — copy into QBR doc
- 0-5 min: Opening + current contract summary (term, ARR, renewal date, payment terms).
- 5-12 min: Health snapshot (usage trends, errors, latency, key metric trends vs baseline).
- 12-22 min: Risk assessment summary (score + top 3 risk drivers).
- 22-30 min: Proposed mitigation plan (owners, timeline, measures of success).
- 30-35 min: Ask & commitment from customer (ROI reminders, case studies).
- 35-40 min: Next steps + follow-up meeting scheduling.

Risk Scoring Rubric (0-50) — composite, higher = more at-risk
- Product Fit & Engagement (0-15): active seats, API call trend, feature usage (weighted 40%).
- Support & Reliability Signals (0-10): sev tickets open in last 90d, incident exposure (weighted 25%).
- Financial & Contract Signals (0-10): past-due invoices, pricing objections, procurement delays (weighted 20%).
- Strategic & Exec Sponsorship (0-15): sponsor health, org changes, M&A signals (weighted 15%).

Quick thresholds (example):
- 0-12: Green (monitor)
- 13-25: Yellow (proactive outreach + product health check)
- 26-50: Red (activate 14-day risk sprint + possible exec involvement)

Evidence checklist for scoring (copy into renewal ticket):
- Last 90d usage chart (product) — include API/throughput per route.
- Top 5 error/latency incidents (SRE notes).
- Billing history + outstanding items.
- Contract owners and procurement status.
- Support case IDs and time-to-first-response trends.
- Recent CSAT/Feedback notes.

14-Day Risk Sprint (owner: CSM) — playbook format
Day 0 (kickoff, immediately after flagged):
- Create a sprint task in Linear and link to renewal ticket. Assign CSM, SE, SRE contact, Renewal Rep.
- Send customer-facing email: 3-pt agenda (acknowledge issue, propose quick wins, schedule deep-dive). Template below.
- Internal sync: 15-min stand to align owners and blockers.

Day 1-7 (technical & adoption plays):
- Play A: Rapid Health Fix (owner: SRE/SE) — triage top 1–2 incidents, provide targeted mitigations (config, rate limits, cache changes). Goal: measurable latency/error reduction within 72h.
- Play B: Targeted Enablement (owner: SE/CSM) — 1-hr working session to remove adoption blockers, implement 1 recommended prompt template or embedding config.
- Play C: Usage Incentive (owner: CSM/Renewals) — offer short-term credit or pilot expansion to redraw usage pattern (align with finance rules).

Day 8-14 (commercial & exec plays):
- Re-assess score and customer sentiment.
- If progress >= defined KPIs => move to renewal negotiation play (standard).
- If insufficient progress => prepare Exec Briefing and escalate per matrix.

Escalation Matrix & Triggers
- Trigger: Score >= 35 OR no progress after 14-day sprint OR exec sponsor withdraws.
- Level 1 (Lead CSM + Renewal Rep) — immediate outreach, commercial concessions discussion.
- Level 2 (CS Director + SE Manager) — 48h to present remediation plan and POC for technical fixes.
- Level 3 (VP CS + CRO) — exec briefing, propose one-time bespoke terms (discount, SLO commitment, Dedicated capacity offer).

Exec Briefing Packet (prepare within 48h) — include these sections:
- One-page summary: current state, risk score, ask (what we need from execs), recommended concession and expected ROI.
- Timeline of interventions to date and evidence (metrics + customer comments).
- Proposed escalation email to customer's exec sponsor (short, clear ask).
- Decision matrix: concession tiers vs. expected close probability uplift.

Sample Exec Email (to customer exec sponsor) — tone: short, constructive
Subject: Partnership check-in ahead of renewal (proposed fix + ask)
Hi [Name],
We value our partnership and want to ensure Redwood is delivering expected outcomes. Following recent issues and our customer success review, we propose a short remediation plan (technical + commercial) to get you back on track before renewal on [date].
Can we schedule a 20-minute exec check-in next week to confirm commitments?
Thanks,
[VP / CRO name]

Commercial Save Plays (examples)
- Conditional Renewal Credit: small fixed credit tied to SLO achievement over next 90d.
- Performance Commitment: Dedicated capacity or SLA upgrade for a defined period with measured KPIs.
- Pilot Expansion with Success Metrics: expand scope for 60d with acceptance criteria and discount if met.

Redwood-specific constraints (notes to CSMs)
- Any commercial concession > 10% ARR must be pre-approved by Renewals Lead and Finance. Use internal approvals workflow.
- Any Dedicated capacity or Private deployment offer must involve Solutions Eng + Legal; add 10 business days to timeline.
- Credit offers must be recorded in Salesforce with a linked contract amendment.

14-7-3-1 Day Communication Cadence (example)
- T-14: Sprint kickoff + working session booked (owner CSM).
- T-7: Sprint retrospective + revised plan (internal + customer).
- T-3: Final negotiation round (commercial team present).
- T-1: Confirmation email + renewal paperwork ready.

Handoff checklist for Renewals Team (post-save)
- Updated renewal contract draft with line items for concessions.
- Signed SOW / amendment if new scope included.
- Confirmation from SRE/SE that technical mitigations are deployed.
- Post-renewal success plan and 30/60/90d milestones.

Operational notes / local tips (CSMs, quick win list)
- Ask for telemetry export (CSV) during QBR; quickest way to validate usage claims.
- If customer cites latency, collect request IDs and top-10 traces before call — SE can usually diagnose in 30–90 minutes.
- Use the "pilot credit" as a bridging instrument rather than a price cut where possible.

Tracking & metrics to record on renewal ticket (minimum)
- Pre- and post-intervention 7d rolling avg latency and error rate.
- Usage delta (active calls/week) before and after enablement session.
- CSAT follow-up score after remediation.
- Final renewal status and reason code (won/lost/accepted-with-changes).

Appendix: Quick templates
- Customer kickoff email (short):
Hi [Customer],
Thanks again for the QBR today. Based on our review we want to run a focused 14-day plan to address the top items. Can you confirm these three owners on your side: [Name product lead], [Name procurement]?
- Internal incident triage note (copy for SRE): include request IDs, timestamps, route names, and customer-facing impact.

Open questions / to-do (notes to self):
- Add standardized Confluence template for exec packet (CS ops backlog).
- Build a simple Linear template for 14-day sprint with pre-populated tasks. Priya -> Linear board owner: Jordan.
- Validate finance approval thresholds with Renewals Lead (Marcus).

References and useful links:
- Renewal runbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.com/display/CS/renewal-runbook
- Escalation Slack channel: #critical-renewals (use only after Level 2 trigger)
- Linear template: https://linear.app/RED/template/renewal-14-day

Last updated notes:
- Drafted initial scoring and sprint flow 2025-11-04 (Priya).
- Added Commercial Save Plays and Exec Email templates 2025-12-10 (Jordan).
- Incorporated SRE triage checklist 2026-01-16 (Samir).

End of doc.
